The prediction network is walked through two steps, because one would not
exercise the recurrence at all *and* would hide a swapped gate order: the
blank's embedding row is zero in this checkpoint, so the first step's gates
come entirely from the bias.

    dec_out    1.8e-04 relative     dec_out1   3.5e-04
    dec_h      1.0e-05              dec_h1     6.4e-04
    dec_c      5.1e-05              dec_c1     4.5e-04
    encoder_projected  1.9e-04
    joint_logits       4.0e-05

The last row is the one to read. An independent numpy computation of the same
product with fp16 operands and fp32 accumulation puts the floor at **3.3e-5**;
the device measures 4.0e-5. There is nothing in that number but the rounding.

The end-to-end assertion is the trace, for S6's reason: the decisions here are
discrete, so either every emission agrees or the port is wrong. It runs twice
— once over the reference's own encoder output (`TestGPUDecodeMatchesReference`,
which isolates the tail) and once over the device's (`TestGPUPipeline`, the
whole vertical) — and both produce 46 emissions at the same frames with the
same durations and the same string.

## What this leaves

    front end     21 ms   48%   <- host FFTs, float64
    encoder       17 ms   40%   (14.3 ms on the device)
    decode         5 ms   12%
    total         43 ms          257x real time

The model is finished. From 2.68 s on the CPU to 43 ms, 62x, with the
transcript unchanged at every step of the way — and the thing that is now half
the pipeline is the one part of it that has never been anything but a
straightforward CPU implementation.

On 2026-09-13 Oliver chose to end the microbenchmark phase and build the
**z-image-turbo vertical slice** (loader → DiT → attention → VAE → PNG) with
real weights, accepting ~20-30 s/image at first. Image generation is the
priority model of the five in `GOALS.md`. Kernel work now continues only
where a profiler points, not where the IDEAS backlog points.

**Why:** after 15+ sessions, `bench/` was 84% of the Go code, every `api/`
endpoint returned `NotImplemented`, no checkpoint had ever been loaded (all
results were against random tensors), and the last iteration bought 1.09x
while attention and convolution sat at zero. The backlog generates new items
faster than it closes them, so it has no convergence criterion.

**How to apply:** prefer finishing a runnable stage over optimising a
measured one. Validate each stage against the diffusers reference rather
than a shape table — that is also what unblocks IDEAS §7 (accuracy), which
has zero work done and gates every format decision.

**Update 2026-09-14:** the z-image slice reached `prompt → PNG` in 14.26 s and
is now **parked**, with its resume points at the top of `PIPELINE.md`. Oliver's
call was to take the two simpler verticals first — speech-to-text
(`parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3`) and text-to-speech (`Kokoro-82M`) — and come back for
the remaining z-image performance after. The current plan lives in
**`SPEECH.md`**, which is now the file to read first.

See [[strix-halo-bench-runs]] for how to run the old benchmark suite, and
[[auto-committer-owns-main]] for why the commit log is not the project's
narrative.

content.text:
Two stages landed this session. Both are validated against the Python reference dump and both leave the transcript byte-identical.

## S7 — the subsampling stack on Vulkan (92 ms → 0.97 ms, 95x)

The port turned out to be a **layout**, not a kernel. Held as PyTorch holds it (`[C, T, F]`) every operator fights the machine; held channel-last as `[T, F, C]`:

- the depthwise convolutions' 256 lanes walk 256 contiguous floats per tap,
- the 1×1 convolutions become `[8832, 256] × [256, 256]` GEMMs on the existing ladder with **no packing pass**,
- the flatten is a 5 µs row copy, once the linear's `[1024, 4096]` weight has its columns permuted at upload.

Three quarters of the stack's arithmetic was already on the ladder. Two things were unexpected: stage 8's implicit-GEMM conv answers the same layout question the *opposite* way because its input has 512 channels and this one has **one**; and the wide four-wave tile lost the 8832-row shape it was built for (N=256 is only four of its tiles wide) — `reg32x32_bt16_w32` wins here too, a third set of shapes on one tile.

## S8 — the transducer tail on Vulkan (208 ms → 4.8 ms, 43x)

The first **latency**-bound stage in the engine: 1.1 GFLOP that took 208 ms because each of 46 emissions was a host round trip. No new GEMM — M=1 runs on the existing rungs with M padded to the tile, and the ladder proves why that's fine: `BM=32` ties `BM=16` **exactly**, twice, reproducibly, doing double the arithmetic for the same time.

The finding is **24 MB of weights against a 32 MiB MALL**. The LSTM and joint GEMMs measure 449 and 702 GB/s — above the DRAM bus — because the loop re-reads the whole model from cache 46 times. First place in the repo where §0.4's 32 MiB budget was *met* rather than fallen off.

One thing that looked like a bug and wasn't: both biases are folded into passes that already read the vector, so the arena holds `W·x` where the reference holds `W·x + b` — a 4.8% relative difference on the joint head, on a tensor whose argmax was already correct.

## Where the clip stands

```
              CPU (S5)    S6     S7     S8
front end        20ms    21ms   25ms   20ms   48%
encoder        2454ms   106ms   20ms   17ms   40%
decode          209ms   206ms  209ms    5ms   12%
total           2.61s   331ms  255ms   42ms
real time        4.2x    33x    43x    261x
```

Same words, same 46 emissions, same frames and durations at every step. `go build`, `gofmt`, `go vet` and the full test suite are clean.

Write-ups in `research/s7-parakeet-subsampling.md` and `research/s8-parakeet-decode.md`; `SPEECH.md` and `TODO.md` rewritten. **The front end is now 48% of the pipeline** — a few thousand float64 FFTs on the host, untouched since S3 — and kokoro (T1–T5) is the next vertical.
